newsitem.title: USA: Late dictator Somoza's belongings up for auction.
newsitem.headline: Late dictator Somoza's belongings up for auction.

text.p: Personal possessions of the late Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza Debayle, including an engraved pistol, will be auctioned in Miami on Saturday.
The pistol, a .38 calibre Astar revolver with gold engraving on a walnut stock, is expected to bring between $800 to $1,200, said Richard Schlom of Sloan's Gallery.
Other items include government documents, photographs of Somoza with world leaders, and books from his library.
A presentation trophy from the U.S. Army's Infantry School at Fort Benning, Georgia, is also for sale, along with a Herb Alpert 33 rpm record signed for Somoza by the musician.
"There's a tremendous amount of interest," Schlom said.
Somoza ruled Nicaragua from 1967 to 1972 and from 1974 until he was ousted by the Sandinista revolution in 1979. He was assassinated in Asuncion, Paraguay, a year later.
The belongings had been in the possession of his longtime companion Dinorah Sampson, who lives in Miami.
